new_jobs.title: Public Health Program Manager I - Communications Manager
new_jobs.description:
Overview

The Public Health Program Manager I - Communications, manages and oversees public health information and communication systems and resources and assists with identifying and providing public health training within the Division of Local Health. The main duties include developing and implementing communication plans, acting as an advisor and supporting district office and public health program projects, elevating examples of Local Health's contributions to public health in Vermont, developing and/or editing communication products, maintaining division webpages and social media accounts, coordinating the work of division web and social media editors, and promoting and integrating health equity and accessibility strategies into communication efforts. The Public Health Program Manager I will also assist with developing and training a diverse public health workforce in communications and public health practice, among other responsibilities. We are committed to building and maintaining a multicultural and diverse workforce, and strive to offer a supportive, professionally challenging, and healthy workplace to our employees.

Examples Of Work Include

Consulting with staff to identify how and when to utilize communications strategies to support or enhance public health practices

Maintaining division's Microsoft SharePoint sites and Teams and related content libraries

Maintaining division webpages and creating a web communication plan

Developing and disseminating division news (internal and external), ensuring information positively represents who we are and what we do

Designing, writing, and/or editing reports, publications, presentations, data briefs, factsheets, flyers, and more

Contributing to strategic planning, priority setting, and emerging issues, including assessing communication or other gaps in programming or service provision through best practice public health strategies

Leading communication activities related to improving health equity, including overseeing interpretation and translation processes

Division Of Local Health - Who We Are

The Division of Local Health works to preserve and improve the equitable social, economic, and environmental conditions necessary to attain the highest level of health and well-being for all, thus ensuring healthy Vermonters. The Division of Local Health is committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and welcoming environment that respects and celebrates every person's strength, assets, and values.  The Division of Local Health is committed to leading organizational change efforts that address avoidable inequities and injustices as we work towards the elimination of health and health care disparities.

TELEWORK

The Department of Health supports a hybrid work environment which combines both in person and remote work. Upon hire, employees work with their supervisor to create a schedule that aligns with the business needs of the unit and complies with State of Vermont policy. We believe a hybrid work environment promotes autonomy and allows for increased flexibility and greater work/life balance.

MISSION

Promote the physical, mental, and social well-being of people in Vermont by advancing equity, protecting against disease and injury, and preparing for health emergencies.

VISION

All people and communities in Vermont have equitable opportunities to achieve their highest level of health and well-being. 

VALUES

Equity: We aim to center health justice and address racism and all forms of oppression in our programs and policies, our approach to collaboration, and how we build and nurture our workforce. 
Collaboration: We engage with staff and partners to understand complex problems and design responsive solutions.
Inclusion: We support a culture of belonging and diversity where people are valued, trusted, and able to be their authentic selves.
Harmony: We endorse a balanced, thoughtful, and intentional work environment that allows employees to care for themselves, their families, and the people they serve.
Data: We strive for scientific excellence and cultural responsiveness in the collection, analysis, sharing and use of data.

Who May Apply

This position, Public Health Program Manager I - Communications Manager (Job Requisition #55424)
, is open to all State employees and external applicants.

If you would like more information about this position, please contact Suzanne.Kelley@vermont.gov

Resumes will not be accepted via e-mail. You must apply online to be considered.

Please note that multiple positions in the same work location may be filled from this job posting.

AHS BACKGROUND CHECKS: Candidates must pass any level of background investigation applicable to the position. In accordance with AHS Policy 4.02, Hiring Standards, Vermont and/or national criminal record checks, as well as DMV and adult and child abuse registry checks, as appropriate to the position under recruitment, will be conducted on candidates, with the exception of those who are current classified state employees seeking transfer, promotion or demotion into an AHS classified position or are persons exercising re-employment (RIF) rights.

Environmental Factors

Duties are performed in both a standard office and field settings. Private means of transportation must be available for required travel. Stress may be anticipated in dealing with emotional situations involving application of programs, especially in dealing with families and in the allocation of program resources.

Minimum Qualifications

Master’s degree in public health, public administration, business administration, environmental science, emergency response, human services, social sciences related fields or health-related fields AND one (1) year or more of experience in public health or human services related programmatic work including experience leading a team or project.

OR

Bachelor’s degree in public health, public administration, business administration, environmental science, emergency response, human services, social sciences related fields or health-related fields AND two (2) years or more of experience in public health or human services related programmatic work including experience leading a team or project.

OR

Two (2) years or more of experience as a Public Health Specialist II.

OR

One (1) year or more of experience as Public Health Specialist III.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience leading a team or project.

Experience in health or public health communication with skills including:

Knowledge and expertise in the development, management, and evaluation of communication plans and campaigns, and the ability to use a health equity lens to improve the impact of messaging and avoid bias and stigmatization

Knowledge of the principles and practices of public health.

Knowledge of educational principles and training procedures.

Ability to take information and create messages for different audiences

Experience with project management and comfort working with subject matter experts and stakeholders, to see projects through to completion

Critical thinking and problem-solving skills with the ability to work in a fast-paced environment where information can change quickly

Strong experience with web editing, social media management, Microsoft Office 365 applications, and the ability to understand and use analytics to drive improvement

Total Compensation

As a State employee you are offered a great career opportunity, but it's more than a paycheck. The State's total compensation package features an outstanding set of employee benefits that are worth about 30% of your total compensation, including:

80% State paid medical premium and a dental plan at no cost for employees and their families
Work/Life balance: 11 paid holidays each year and a generous leave plan
State Paid Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FMLI)
Two ways to save for your retirement: A State defined benefit pension plan and a deferred compensation 457(b) plan
Tuition Reimbursement

Low cost group life insurance
Incentive-based Wellness Program
Qualified Employer for Public Service Student Loan Forgiveness Program

Want the specifics? Explore the Benefits of State Employment on our website.

Equal Opportunity Employer

The State of Vermont celebrates diversity, and is committed to providing an environment of mutual respect and meaningful inclusion that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. The State does not discriminate in employment on the basis of race, color, religion or belief, national, social or ethnic origin, sex (including pregnancy), age, physical, mental or sensory disability, HIV Status, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, marital, civil union or domestic partnership status, past or present military service, membership in an employee organization, family medical history or genetic information, or family or parental status. Stepful is a workforce platform redefining how America's largest health systems build, train, and retain their talent. Since our founding in 2021, Stepful’s trained over 32,000 practice-ready healthcare workers.

Join Our Team and Make a Difference!

Employer:
Maybridge Development LLC
Location:
Asheville, NC and surrounding National Forest districts (Brevard, Nebo, Mars Hill, Franklin, Pisgah Forest, Murphy, Robbinsville)
Position:
Full-Time (40 hours/week)

Immediate

6 Positions

About the Role

Maybridge Development LLC is preparing to provide program and project management services to the USDA Forest Service in support of Hurricane Helene recovery efforts across the National Forests in North Carolina.

We are building a team of Program Managers who want to do meaningful work that leaves a lasting impact. This is an opportunity to be part of restoring public lands, strengthening local communities, and supporting the long-term recovery of forests and infrastructure affected by Hurricane Helene.
Projects may include roadway and trail repairs, bridge and culvert replacements, recreation site restoration, facility repairs, hazard tree mitigation, watershed stabilization, and other infrastructure recovery efforts following Hurricane Helene.

Working alongside USDA Forest Service personnel, contractors, and partner agencies, you'll spend time throughout some of North Carolina's most beautiful national forests while helping coordinate projects that serve the public for generations to come. If you enjoy solving complex challenges, collaborating with diverse teams, and being part of something bigger than yourself, this is an opportunity to make a real difference.

As a Federal Disaster Recovery Program Manager, you'll plan, coordinate, and manage assigned recovery projects to ensure work is delivered safely, on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with federal quality and documentation standards.

Key Responsibilities

●      Manage assigned recovery projects from planning through closeout, including scheduling, resource coordination, risk management, budget tracking, and performance monitoring.
●      Maintain project documentation, including project registers, risk logs, stakeholder engagement logs, meeting minutes, and weekly and monthly status reports.
●      Coordinate with USDA Forest Service Staff Officers, partner agencies, consultants, and contractor teams to support successful project delivery.
●      Attend twice-weekly in-person coordination meetings at the USDA Forest Service Supervisor's Office in Asheville.
●      Support the implementation and maintenance of Project Management Plans, the USDA Forest Service FSM 2030 Large-Scale Event Recovery Framework, project documentation, and standard operating procedures (SOPs).
●      Provide project management and standard operating procedure training for NFsNC employees.
●    Conduct field visits throughout National Forest districts, including travel on unpaved and remote forest roads.
●      Identify project risks and develop practical solutions to keep projects on track while maintaining compliance with federal requirements.

Minimum Qualifications

●      Bachelor's degree in Project Management, Business, Natural Resources, Environmental Science, Construction Management, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and professional project management experience.
●      Minimum of five (5) years of experience managing multiple concurrent projects with demonstrated success in scheduling, risk management, stakeholder engagement, resource allocation, and reporting.
●      Strong organizational, communication, and leadership skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
●      U.S. citizen and eligible to obtain and maintain a Federal Tier 1 or Tier 2 Background Investigation.
●      Ability to attend twice-weekly meetings in Asheville and travel throughout Western North Carolina.
●      Proficiency with Microsoft Project, SharePoint, Microsoft Office, and other project management software.
●      Applicants should have access to a reliable four-wheel-drive or high-clearance vehicle suitable for travel on unpaved forest roads. Business-use automobile insurance is recommended.

Preferred Qualifications

●      Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or equivalent.
●      Experience supporting the USDA Forest Service or another federal land management agency.
●      Experience with disaster recovery programs, including FEMA Public Assistance (PA), CDBG-DR, USACE, or similar federally funded recovery initiatives.
●      Familiarity with the USDA Forest Service FSM 2030 Large-Scale Event Recovery Framework.
●      FEMA ICS/NIMS certifications.
●      Experience using Survey123, ArcGIS, or other GIS applications.
●      Residency in Western North Carolina is preferred.

Compensation & Benefits

Salary: $85,000–$90,000
, based on experience, certifications, and relevant federal project experience. Placement within the salary range will be based on qualifications, certifications, and demonstrated success managing federal or disaster recovery projects.
Business mileage is reimbursed at the IRS standard rate under an accountable plan. Commuting between home and the regular work location is not reimbursable. ﻿
Benefits include:
●      Health insurance
●      Paid Time Off (PTO)
●      Eleven (11) paid Federal holidays
●      Mileage reimbursement

Why Join Maybridge?

At Maybridge, we believe great projects leave more than completed work—they leave stronger communities. This is an opportunity to help restore public lands, improve recreation access, and support the long-term recovery of Western North Carolina following Hurricane Helene.
You'll work alongside dedicated professionals from the USDA Forest Service, partner agencies, and the private sector while spending time in some of the state's most remarkable national forests. If you're looking for a career that combines leadership, purpose, and the opportunity to make a lasting impact, we'd love to have you on our team.

Intro/Program Description:
Lincoln Square Neighborhood Center (LSNC) is a multigenerational program of Goddard Riverside, dedicated to meeting the educational, recreational, and cultural aspirations of the Lincoln Square community, with a primary focus on residents of Amsterdam Houses and Amsterdam Addition. Founded by the New York City Department for the Aging (DFTA) and the New York State Office for the Aging (SOFA), LSNC Aging Services provide comprehensive support to over 800 active members, fostering health, engagement, and social connection. Older adults (ages 60+) benefit from daily nutritious hot lunches, wellness programs promoting physical and mental health, educational and arts programming to encourage lifelong learning and social services. Naturally Occurring Retirement Community (NORC) or LSNC NORC specifically serves residents aged 60+ living in the Amsterdam Houses and Amsterdam Addition—NYC Housing Authority (NYCHA) development. NORC enhances aging in place by offering social services (case management, benefits assistance, and advocacy), health promotion (collaboration with onsite nurses, wellness screenings, and health education), recreational, cultural, and social opportunities to foster community engagement and reduce isolation.

Purpose of Position:
The NORC Program Manager provides strategic leadership and operational oversight for the Lincoln Square Neighborhood Center (LSNC) Naturally Occurring Retirement Community (NORC) Supportive Services Program. This position is responsible for the planning, implementation, and supervision of all NORC program components, including social services, outreach, health and wellness programming, community engagement, and partnerships. The role oversees staff and consultants, manages program operations and budgets, coordinates program activities and special events, and ensures compliance with agency policies and funding requirements. The NORC Program Manager works collaboratively with internal teams, healthcare providers, and community partners to support older adults in aging safely and independently in their homes, while fostering a vibrant and inclusive community environment. The NORC Program Manager works in close strategic partnership with the LSNC West 65th Street Older Adult Center (OAC) Director to ensure alignment and integration of services across LSNC Aging Services. This collaboration supports coordinated programming, shared outreach strategies, and the efficient use of resources to expand engagement, strengthen service delivery, and enhance the overall continuum of care for older adults served by both the NORC and OAC programs.

new_jobs.description:
The Data Analyst
will review and analyze data. The Data Analyst will create reports, dashboards, and presentations for stakeholders and/or leadership and utilize findings to aid in decision-making.

Specific Duties & Responsibilities

Collect and analyze quantitative and qualitative data in accordance with applicable privacy laws such as FERPA/HIPAA.
Communicate findings compellingly and visually through dashboards, reports, briefing decks, stories, scorecards, executive briefings, etc. For different audiences using solutions like Power BI and Tableau. Proofread and edit reports and other products to attain consistency of format.
Regular outreach to offices to learn about upcoming surveys scheduled; maintain up to date documentation.
Assist with the development of a detailed communication strategy and plan for the office/assigned area.
Maintain office website and produce materials in coordination with the divisional communications team.
Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree.
Three years of related experience.
Additional education may substitute for required experience, and additional related experience may substitute for required education beyond a high school diploma/graduation equivalent, to the extent permitted by the JHU equivalency formula.

Experience using software for data analysis (Tableau, Power BI, Excel).
